style.summary:
style of A: A answers with short backchannels such as Mm-hmm and Yeah and gives a plain, modest admission of not knowing.
style of B: B speaks in longer, hedged turns full of fillers, with a measured advisory tone that sets the terms of the advice.

A: A's brief acknowledgements keep the floor open, so B has to fill the silence with the substance of the advice.
A's plain admission of not knowing hands B the role of the one who must supply a way forward.
A's terse replies never contest B's view, so A can withhold objection and keep the option of rejecting the advice later.
B: B's hedged but authoritative framing lets B recommend a course of action without being challenged.
B's longer turns carry the substance and steer the exchange toward a short-term conclusion.
B's conditional phrasing places the next step on A's own knowledge, so A's response depends on B's judgement.

A: Brief acknowledgements give A little leverage, because B's long turns decide the direction without A ever pressing the point.
Admitting ignorance makes B the expert whose advice settles the outcome, so B's view is what counts.
A cannot end the exchange on A's own terms, since B holds the floor and decides when the matter is closed.
B: A's continued agreement and admitted ignorance mean B's recommendation rests entirely on A accepting it, so A keeps the final say.
B's long, uncertain turns with fillers show B searching for the right words, so A's brief reactions shape where the point lands.
The condition B names is A's own knowledge, so A decides whether a strong idea exists and therefore which path is taken.

content.summary:
content of A: A's contribution is a single admission that the speaker has no idea what is wrong, which adds almost no substance.
content of B: B supplies the substance, describing the topic as complicated and advising a long-term look once the short-term rush for results ends.

A: A's admission of having no idea leaves B to decide what the technical substance should be.
A's brief reply supplies little content, so the information on the table comes almost entirely from B.
A's open-ended lack of knowledge makes B's advice the only concrete guidance, which gives A the choice of whether to adopt it.
B: B introduces the framing that the topic is complicated, which sets the terms for everything that follows.
B distinguishes the long-term investigation from the short-term need for results, so B defines the priorities.
B's conditional about strong ideas makes the content depend on B's assessment of what is worth pursuing.

A: B's admission that the topic is complicated is hedged, so A's counter-view of simplicity can still reframe the content.
A's few words are a clear statement of what A does not know, and that honesty limits B's ability to shape the substance.
A's choice of whether to adopt the advice is only hypothetical, since B's recommendation has already been put forward as the working plan.
B: B's framing is a general remark that A can counter, so the framing does not fix the substance.
The priority between long term and short term is B's personal judgement, and A can argue the immediate need is the real priority.
B's assessment depends on A's knowledge that is not provided, so the decision of what is worth pursuing rests on A.

coordination.summary:
coordination of A: A gives short backchannels and an interjection, leaving B to hold most of the turns.
coordination of B: B holds the longer turns, pauses mid-thought and restarts, and ends the sequence with a hanging dash.

A: A's Mm-hmm turns let A confirm understanding without taking the floor, which keeps A in control of when to speak.
A's interjection of I don't know at all cuts into B's turn and shifts the discussion to A's situation.
A's short replies keep B's turns going, so B reveals more of B's intentions before A responds.
B: B holds the floor for most of the exchange, which gives B control over how the topic unfolds.
B's trailing dash leaves the turn-taking open, so B decides when the conversation moves on.
B's extended advice shapes the transition from complicated to short term, so B controls the topic shifts.

A: A's backchannels do not interrupt B, so B continues to hold the floor and decides when the sequence ends.
A's interjection is brief and B resumes at once, which shows B reclaims the floor and keeps the transition under B's control.
B's long turns reveal intentions that A simply accepts, so B's plan determines the course of the exchange.
B: B's trailing dash shows B failed to complete the thought, so A can take over the next move.
B's long turns are interrupted by A's reply I don't know at all, which breaks B's control of the topic shift.
B's transitions are only proposed, and A can decline to follow them.

engagement.summary:
engagement of A: A is minimally engaged, offering agreement and an honest admission of not knowing the subject.
engagement of B: B is engaged in the problem, offering a considered view that the topic deserves future attention.

A: A's honest admission of ignorance invites B to explain, which keeps A in the position of learner and sets the pace.
A's agreement signals keep B engaged, which lets A influence the level of B's involvement.
A's willingness to be guided gives A the choice of whether to take up B's suggestions.
B: B's suggestion to look into it in the longer term shows B's interest and makes B the one who sets the agenda.
B's careful framing of the problem as complicated shows investment, which gives B more authority over the outcome.
B's conditional invitation to A places the decision on A and makes B the engaged party who holds the next step.

A: A's agreement signals are passive, and B's engagement is what actually drives the exchange forward.
B's engagement is evident in long turns, so the pace is set by B rather than by A's signals.
A's option to take up suggestions is only nominal, since B's advice already defines what the next step will be.
B: B's suggestion is a long-term aside, and A's immediate lack of knowledge is what the conversation actually turns on.
B's careful framing is a hedge that does not commit B, so A's honest uncertainty holds more weight.
B's invitation depends on A's knowledge, so the decision and the engagement that matters sit with A.
